title: QuantumChain: Blockchain-Backed Quantum Federated Learning for Financial Fraud Detection
authors: Epameinondas Douros, Konstantinos Dalampekis, Nouhaila Innan, Ioannis Theodonis, Muhammad Shafique
abstract: Financial fraud detection is challenged by decentralized data, severe class imbalance, and privacy constraints. This paper presents QuantumChain, a secure Quantum Federated Learning (QFL) framework that combines hybrid quantum-classical neural networks, encrypted federated aggregation, blockchain-based auditability, and quantum-secure communication. Each client trains a local hybrid model in which a variational quantum circuit is embedded between classical neural layers, while model updates are protected through homomorphic encryption, threshold secret sharing, and QKD-based keying. A permissioned blockchain records aggregation events and supports reputation-weighted trust among participants. We evaluate QuantumChain on financial transaction data using a compact, size-matched classical baseline to isolate the effect of the quantum layer. Results show that the HQNN achieves comparable accuracy while improving fraud-class recall in most settings, reaching 94.6% recall compared with 93.2% for the classical model. The Deep QLayer improves performance in full-data settings, suggesting that added circuit depth helps recover representational capacity when the shallow circuit becomes limited. Mixed-state simulations further show that the recall trend persists under non-ideal quantum evolution. In federated deployment with 10 heterogeneous clients, global accuracy increases from 97.7% to 98.8% over five rounds before stabilizing. These results show that QuantumChain can integrate depth-aware hybrid quantum models into a secure federated fraud-detection pipeline while maintaining stable global convergence.
summary: This paper introduces QuantumChain, a novel framework that applies Quantum Federated Learning to solve financial fraud detection under strict privacy constraints. It combines hybrid quantum-classical neural networks with advanced security measures like homomorphic encryption and blockchain auditing. The results demonstrate that this secure, quantum-enhanced approach improves detection recall over purely classical methods.
main_problem: The paper addresses financial fraud detection, which is complicated by decentralized data, class imbalance, and strict privacy requirements.
main_result: The proposed QuantumChain framework successfully integrates hybrid quantum models into a secure federated learning pipeline, achieving improved fraud-class recall over classical baselines while maintaining stable global convergence.
method: It employs a multi-layered security protocol combining Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks (HQNNs), homomorphic encryption, threshold secret sharing, and blockchain auditing for privacy and integrity.
model_or_system: The core model is the QuantumChain framework utilizing HQNNs, which embed variational quantum circuits between classical neural layers. Security relies on QKD-derived keys and a permissioned blockchain ledger.
key_observables: Fraud-class recall (primary metric), global accuracy, and the Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER) for security checks.
important_parameters: Federated rounds (e.g., 5 rounds), client count (10 heterogeneous clients), circuit depth (Shallow vs. Deep QLayer).
main_assumptions: The blockchain layer is simulated using a local Ethereum/Ganache environment, and QKD security relies on pre-shared credentials or digital signatures for authentication.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the overall QuantumChain process flow (local training to aggregation), compare Shallow vs. Deep QLayer architectures, and show performance results across different settings.
paper_structure: The paper details the architecture of QuantumChain, outlines the multi-step protocol involving local quantum training, secure update transmission via encryption/QKD, blockchain commitment, and final server-side aggregation.
why_interesting: While applied to finance, the core mechanism involves embedding variational quantum circuits into a deep learning structure (HQNN) for computation, which is relevant to NISQ device applications in quantum machine learning theory.
